title: Weekly Engineering Sync
overview: The SSO login flow is built, but testing is blocked on an Okta sandbox tenant; Priya will get it approved today.
Transcript virtualization shipped: a 3-hour meeting now loads in under half a second instead of about 4 seconds.
A click-to-seek timestamp drift bug (milliseconds vs seconds rounding) will be fixed before Thursday's release.
Code freeze is Wednesday at noon; the release includes virtualization, the timestamp fix and player keyboard shortcuts.
On-call passes from Marcus to Aisha; the export service needs a proper streaming solution for large PDFs.

comments.body: This is the bug customers reported in support ticket #4821.

transcript: Priya Sharma: Morning all. Let's keep this to fifteen minutes. Quick round of updates, then blockers, then the release plan for Thursday. Marcus, want to start?

Marcus Chen: Sure. I finished the SAML assertion parsing and the login redirect flow. The part I'm stuck on is testing. We still don't have an Okta sandbox tenant, so I'm testing against a mock identity provider.
Priya Sharma: How long have you been waiting on the sandbox?
Marcus Chen: About a week. IT said it needs a manager's approval because it's a paid tenant.
Priya Sharma: Okay, that's on me. I'll request the Okta sandbox from IT today and approve it myself.
Marcus Chen: Thanks. The other thing is the sessions table. We need a migration to store the identity provider on each session, and I want to write it so it's backwards compatible with the old login.
Priya Sharma: Makes sense. Write the migration this week and let's review it together before it goes anywhere near production.
Ravi Patel: My turn. I shipped the transcript virtualization, so long meetings now render only the visible lines. A three hour meeting went from about four seconds to load to under half a second.
Aisha Bello: I can confirm that, it's a huge difference. I tested it on the biggest customer meeting we have and scrolling is smooth now.

Ravi Patel: There's one bug I found though. When you click a transcript line, the player sometimes jumps one or two seconds before the actual timestamp. It looks like a rounding issue between milliseconds and seconds.
Priya Sharma: Is that a regression from the virtualization work?
Ravi Patel: I don't think so, I see it on the old version too. But it's more noticeable now because the active line highlight is more precise. I'll fix the timestamp drift before Thursday's release.
Aisha Bello: From QA, the regression suite is green except for two flaky tests in the calendar sync. They fail maybe once in ten runs, always on a timezone edge case.
Marcus Chen: That's probably daylight saving time. The test creates a meeting at two AM on the day the clocks change.
Aisha Bello: That would explain it. I'll pin the test clock to a fixed date and see if the flakiness goes away.
Priya Sharma: Good. Now the release on Thursday. What's going in?
Ravi Patel: Transcript virtualization, the timestamp fix if it's ready, and the new keyboard shortcuts for the player. Space to play and pause, and the arrow keys to skip five seconds.
Aisha Bello: I'd like a code freeze on Wednesday at noon so I have a full afternoon for the regression pass.
Priya Sharma: Agreed, code freeze Wednesday noon. Ravi, please also update the release notes, since most of the changes are yours.
Ravi Patel: Sure, I'll update the release notes tomorrow.
Priya Sharma: Last thing, on-call. Marcus is handing over to Aisha this week. Anything she should know?
Marcus Chen: Only one incident this week. The export service ran out of memory on a very large PDF export. I added a page limit as a quick fix, but we need a proper streaming solution.
Priya Sharma: Let's create a ticket for the streaming export and pick it up next sprint. Thanks everyone, see you Thursday.
